The word erection comes from the verb "to erect," which means to raise, build, or set something upright. Keeping that root meaning in mind will help you understand every sense of this word naturally.
Meaning 1 — The Act of Building or Putting Something Up

This is the most common and general meaning. An erection is the process of constructing or setting up a structure — raising it from nothing into a standing position.

Examples:

  • "The erection of the bridge took two full years."
  • "The erection of the new hospital was finally completed last month."
  • "The erection of a fence around the property kept the animals out."

Think of it as the event of something being built or raised. It applies to buildings, monuments, walls, tents, scaffolding, statues — anything that is assembled and made to stand upright.
Meaning 2 — A Structure That Has Been Built

Erection can also refer to the finished structure itself — the thing that was erected. In this sense, it is simply another word for a building or a constructed object.

Examples:

  • "The tower is an impressive erection of stone and iron."
  • "The ancient temple is the most remarkable erection in the entire city."

This usage is more formal and somewhat old-fashioned. You will encounter it more in older texts, legal documents, and formal writing than in everyday conversation.

This is the anatomical and medical meaning of the word. In biology and medicine, an erection refers to a state in which soft tissue in the body becomes firm, enlarged, and rigid because blood rushes into and fills it.

This most commonly refers to a penile erection — when the penis stiffens and becomes enlarged. Here is exactly how and why it happens:

  • Inside the penis, there are sponge-like chambers of tissue called the corpora cavernosa.
  • When a person is sexually aroused (or sometimes during sleep, or even randomly without a clear cause), the nervous system sends signals that relax the blood vessels leading into these chambers.
  • Blood flows in rapidly and fills them up.
  • The pressure of the blood filling these tissues causes the penis to become firm, enlarged, and to point outward or upward.
  • The erection ends when the blood drains back out.

This is a completely normal and involuntary physiological process, meaning the body does it on its own — a person does not consciously control it in the way they might move their hand.

The clitoris (in female anatomy) also becomes erect through the exact same mechanism — blood fills its internal tissue and it becomes firmer and slightly enlarged. This is called a clitoral erection, though the change is far less visually obvious than a penile erection because most of the clitoris is internal.

Examples in medical/anatomical context:

  • "An erection is a normal part of male sexual response."
  • "Difficulty achieving an erection can sometimes indicate an underlying health condition."

All three meanings share the same underlying logic — something that was soft, flat, or non-existent is raised upright and made firm or standing. Whether it is a building rising from the ground or tissue filling with blood and stiffening, the concept of raising something to an upright, firm state is at the heart of every use of this word.
Register and Usage — When to Use Which Meaning

ContextMeaning in play
Construction, architecture, engineeringMeanings 1 or 2
Medicine, biology, sex educationMeaning 3
Formal/legal documentsAny of the three
Everyday conversationMeaning 3 (Meanings 1 & 2 are now rare in casual speech)

Practical note: In modern everyday speech, when people say "an erection" without any construction context, they almost always mean the anatomical sense (Meaning 3). The construction meanings are still perfectly correct and used in professional/formal writing, but they have become less common in casual conversation precisely because Meaning 3 is so dominant in everyday usage.

Erection as a noun means either (1) the act of constructing and raising a structure, (2) a structure that has been built, or (3) the physiological state in which soft bodily tissue — most commonly the penis or clitoris — becomes firm and enlarged due to blood flowing into it. All three meanings share the root idea of something being raised to an upright, firm state. In formal and technical writing, all three meanings are actively used. In everyday conversation, the anatomical meaning is the dominant one.
